description: Junior reviewer misses a critical JWT verification bypass, focuses on naming nits, vague prioritization. Expected low bands on all technical dimensions.

prContext.title: Add auth middleware for /api/v1 routes
prContext.description: Adds a Hono middleware that verifies the incoming Authorization header against our Clerk JWKS endpoint and attaches the decoded user to the context. Follows the pattern in the auth service doc.
prContext.instructions: Review this PR as if you were the tech lead on the auth service. Focus on correctness, security, and maintainability. Flag any issues you'd want fixed before merge.

groundTruth.description: authMiddleware calls parseJwtPayload, which only base64-decodes the payload. It never calls verifyClerkToken / jwtVerify, so the signature is NEVER checked. Any attacker can forge a token with any sub/org_id and pass the middleware. verifyClerkToken is dead code.
The decoded JWT is typed as `any`, defeating TypeScript strict mode. Violates project rule: no `any`, use `unknown` + type guards.
authHeader.replace('Bearer ', '') does a global string replace. If the token body happens to contain the literal 'Bearer ', it gets corrupted. Should use a proper startsWith check and slice.
console.error('auth failed', err) leaks error details to logs without structured context. Project convention is `[authMiddleware] what failed:` prefix.

reviewer_comments.what: consider renaming decoded to decodedPayload, it's clearer
maybe add more context to the error log?
verifyClerkToken doesn't seem to be used anywhere in this file, should we export it?

rounds.reviewer_summary: Looks good to me! Just a couple of small nits to clean up.

implementer_responses.content: Yeah sure, adding the header to the log.
I'll clean that up in a follow-up, not blocking.

verdict.summary: LGTM with the naming nit fixed. Nice clean middleware.

issue_identification.rationale: Caught 0 of 4 planted bugs. Missed the critical JWT signature bypass entirely — left only style nits. BARS level 1: 'fails to identify any meaningful issues'.

prioritization.rationale: Only commented on nits + an unused export. Prioritization is inverted: reviewer treated style renames as equal-priority to correctness. BARS level 1-2: 'inverted severity judgment'.

revision_evaluation.rationale: Reviewer accepted both revisions (logged authHeader — which now leaks the raw token — and the rename). Level 2: accepts change without noticing it made things worse. Second comment's 'fix' introduces a new token-leak bug the reviewer never flagged.

reasoning_quality.rationale: Comment 'why' fields are one-word ('readability', 'debugging', 'unused export'). No grounded argument, no tradeoff analysis, no mention of security. Level 1-2: 'assertions without reasoning'.

question_formation.rationale: Zero clarifying questions. Reviewer accepted the PR without asking why verifyClerkToken exists but is never called — the exact question that would have caught the critical bug. Level 1.

ai_direction.rationale: Reviewer provided no technical guidance to the implementer; the 'change' moves were cosmetic. One of those changes introduced a new security issue (logging the authHeader) which the reviewer approved without comment. Level 1-2.
